title: Boiling Water Clears PVC Drain Clogs: Myth vs. Fact
description: A common DIY belief is that pouring boiling water down a sink drain is a safe, easy method to dissolve stubborn grease clogs. However, boiling water reaches 212°F (100°C), which exceeds the maximum recommended continuous service temperature of standard PVC drain-waste-vent piping, typically around 140°F (60°C). Repeated exposure to near-boiling water can soften pipe walls, compromise solvent-welded joints, or distort rubber seals in slip joints. Professional plumbers rely on mechanical drain cables or hydro-jetting to clear grease safely without risking thermal damage to the drainage assembly. Always verify piping materials before applying high heat.

Boiling Water Clears PVC Drain Clogs: Myth vs. Fact

A common DIY belief is that pouring boiling water down a sink drain is a safe, easy method to dissolve stubborn grease clogs. However, boiling water reaches 212°F (100°C), which exceeds the maximum recommended continuous service temperature of standard PVC drain-waste-vent piping, typically around 140°F (60°C). Repeated exposure to near-boiling water can soften pipe walls, compromise solvent-welded joints, or distort rubber seals in slip joints. Professional plumbers rely on mechanical drain cables or hydro-jetting to clear grease safely without risking thermal damage to the drainage assembly. Always verify piping materials before applying high heat.
